sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was front-loaded: revenue rose 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then slowed to 0.1% in FY2023 before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 loss of $3,445.1 million was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the IPO-related RSU performance condition and the CEO award [F32][P74].
The operating loss narrowed from $1,398.4 million in FY2023 to $532.2 million in FY2025, lifting operating margin from -30.4% to -9.0% [F18][F20][F28][F30].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth, versus 3.7pp from Rest of world [D456][D458][D499][D406].
Advertising was 87.4% of FY2025 revenue and grew 5.8%, contributing 5.3pp, while Other revenue grew 62.9% and contributed 5.4pp [D536][D537][D538][D544][D545].
The FY2025 advertising gain came from roughly 17% more impressions, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression, and other revenue rose on subscription growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth in FY2025, an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
Diluted shares rose 2.1% in FY2025, so the 35.7% smaller loss per share trailed the 34.0% smaller net loss [D425][D410][D408].
FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a window median of -32.4% and low of -422.5% in FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The FY2025 bridge was led by cost of revenue adding 1.1pp, R&D 1.3pp and other lines 3.3pp as each fell as a share of revenue [D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
Net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above operating margin, helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [F50][F30][D591][P18].
Against internet peers (n=5) the FY2025 operating margin sits at the 0th percentile versus a 20.3% median [D570][D571].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million in FY2025 both exceed the $460.5 million net loss, a 7.4% free-cash-flow margin [F80][F100][F40][D393].
Operating cash flow rose on the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A, plus working-capital timing [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, up from a 2.8% revenue share in FY2022 [F90][D392][D395][D249].
Capex is primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Net cash swung from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, or -10.1% of revenue [D211][D399][D400].
That net-cash position ranks at the 0th percentile against internet peers (n=5), whose median is 45.0% of revenue [D578][D579].
The FY2025 shift reflects $1.4 billion of note repurchases funded by $1.47 billion of new 2033 Notes, plus $750.9 million of buybacks [P1][P2][X156].
Buybacks were 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D402][D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last 10 years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of FY2025 revenue and has been at least 10% in each of the last 9 years [R2][D390].
Net cash has fallen for four straight years into net debt, reaching -$596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025 [R4][D402].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the FY2025 high of -9.0% or slips back toward the -32.4% median [F30][D554][D555].
Whether free cash flow margin stays above the FY2025 high of 7.4% or falls back toward the -4.1% median [D560][D561].
Whether net cash returns above zero from -$596.3 million in FY2025, given buybacks at 171.7% of free cash flow [D399][D402].
